messages:
maria: quick follow-up from today's kernel RFC sync — we need a concrete plan for a hybrid Triton/CUTLASS rollout. high-level goal: pick best-performing kernel per attention shape while keeping a single runtime path and simple fallbacks.

jin: agreed. current problems: maintenance cost of two code paths, inconsistent perf for narrow vs wide seqlen, and testing gaps.

sam: +1. propose we define a small adapter interface so runtime can select impl by op signature, not by model. keeps placement logic centralized.

riley: can we avoid binary bloat? two kernels + extra dispatch layers might increase binary size and load time on cold start.

dmitri: we should measure. add microbench for cold start memory and load time. also quantify peak GPU memory delta between CUTLASS quantized kernels vs Triton mixed-precision.

maria: action items draft: 1) adapter interface RFC (owner: jin) — spec + minimal shim. 2) perf harness (owner: dmitri) — microbench + long-run throughput. 3) CI gates (owner: sam) — perf regression checks and rollout automation. 4) canary plan (owner: riley) — A/B by traffic slice. due: 2 weeks.

jin: I'll sketch adapter interface. rough idea: a small trait with selectors: op_key -> implementation_id, and a capability query (supports_kv_cache, supports_rotary, max_block_k).

jin: pseudo:```
interface KernelAdapter {
  select(op_key: String, shape: ShapeMeta): ImplId
  query_capability(impl: ImplId, feature: String): bool
  warmup(impl: ImplId): Result
}
```

sam: looks good. add a compatibility matrix: which models/ops must always prefer Triton for numerical parity. also add a fallback that logs once per minute for mismatches.

riley: for canary we should route by model + request size. 5% traffic to hybrid, 95% to current CUTLASS-only baseline. escalate on p99 latency bump >10% or regressed quality on eval set.

ops-bot: note: incident policy link https://redwood.internal/ops/incidents #auto

dmitri: for perf harness: I'll include these benchmarks:
- attention shapes: (seq=16, head=64), (seq=512, head=64), (seq=2048, head=32), variable batch sizes 1..32
- metrics: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU mem, kernel launch count, nvprof traces

maria: good. also capture KV cache warmup behavior — prefix cache hits should be measured (cold vs warm). add an integration test that runs a short convo and checks logits near-identical within epsilon 1e-3.

sam: CI gating idea: run microbench on a GPU pool for PRs that touch runtime or kernel selector. perf thresholds stored in a small YAML in repo. ci-bot will post result summary. if regress >5% on critical shapes, block merge.

ci-bot: @sam i'll add a job template. sample config:```
jobs:
  kernel_perf:
    runs-on: gpu-small
    matrix: shapes: [s16_h64, s512_h64, s2048_h32]
    threshold-file: kernels/bench/thresholds.yaml
```

riley: we need rollout checklist: health dashboards, synthetic canary load generator, automatic rollback, and a human in the loop for first 24h. i'll draft.

dmitri: small nit — for CUTLASS we rely on custom epilogue kernels for best perf. adapter must allow passing epilogue params through so we don't lose perf.

jin: noted. adapter will carry a small opaque config blob for impl-specific params. keep it minimal.

maria: QA/acceptance: 1) perf non-regression on critical shapes, 2) numerical parity on eval prompt set, 3) no increase in mean cold-start time > 10%.

sam: owners ok with deadlines? jin/dmitri/sam/riley — two-week drafts, final PRs in 4 weeks.

riley: ack. i'll create the canary repo and traffic-split job tomorrow.

dmitri: starting perf harness work today, will post baseline numbers by EOD Friday.

maria: thanks all. tagging follow-ups: @jin (adapter), @dmitri (bench), @sam (CI), @riley (canary). we'll reconvene next Wed. :calendar:

ci-bot: scheduled reminder: architecture sync follow-up meeting set for 1799520000 - sent to channel.
